title: Final verification: detect an error, restore a copy and retain the source
goal: Independently reconcile, perform a discriminating negative control and actually restore the final work.
prerequisites: 1c-enterprise.a 7; A1–A2: separate infobase, catalogs, references and documents; synthetic data only.
outcomes: 455/difference15 and restored identities with source retained.
sections: UI checks show action reachability; data checks show persisted correctness; recovery checks show backup usability. None replaces the others. Map case IDs to requirements and expected states. Preserve each failure before fixing it so the cause remains explainable.

List actual 12 request numbers and durations and calculate 440 independently. Compare membership, not totals alone: losing 30 and adding another 30 can preserve the sum. Equal names need identity checks. Do not derive both observed and expected values from the same report query.
Independence does not require complex tools

A separate manual identity-and-total table suffices for 12 documents. Do not derive expectations from the same query being checked. Compare membership, totals and units. Deliberately omit one record in an experimental report: reconciliation should identify the missing key and difference, not merely display FAIL.

In a separate copy change the final 65 to 80, giving 455 while the accepted source remains 440. Identify the exact number and 15-minute difference. Also test missing customer or 1441 with refusal and unchanged saved state. Do not destroy source records to manufacture a failure.
Recovery checks both source and copy

Dump the agreed state and restore it to a new directory. Reconcile identities and values after a fresh session. Change only the restored copy, then reread the source. Equal customer names are insufficient: duplicates with different references can look identical. Preserve provenance and source hashes separately from private infobase files.

Close Enterprise, dump a DT and restore only into another empty base/directory. Compare 12 identities, references, minutes, statuses and your added attribute. Change only the restored copy and reread the source. A JSON snapshot or archive existence does not replace actual recovery.

If the edition restricts runtime report export, use a permitted protocol and state the limit. An unperformed restore leaves a critical gate open. A local self-check verifies neither identity nor instructor grading. A useful final record separates proven outcomes, failures and remaining work.

Record PASS/FAIL/NOT RUN for each case. Training-edition printing/server limits are separate. Self-checks establish neither identity/authorship nor teacher grading. If critical recovery is untested, the work remains incomplete even after theory completion.
